subject: physics
source_note: Topic structure follows the IB Diploma Physics guide (first assessment 2025), organised under themes A–E. Topic names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

units.name: D — Fields

units.name: E — Nuclear and Quantum Physics
units.blurb: The atom, quantum physics, radioactivity and stars

topics.blurb: Reference frames, time dilation and length contraction

topics.name: B.4 Thermodynamics (HL)

connections.why: Kinematics describes the motion that forces produce
Forces acting through distances do work and transfer energy
Torque is the rotational analogue of force in rigid bodies
Classical kinematics is the low-speed limit of special relativity
A restoring force produces the oscillation of simple harmonic motion
Gravitational force provides the centripetal force for orbits
Energy conservation extends to thermal energy transfers
Electrical power is energy transferred per unit time in circuits
Work and energy underpin the first law of thermodynamics
Thermal energy relates to the kinetic energy of gas particles
Radiative thermal transfer underlies the greenhouse effect
Gas behaviour is analysed through thermodynamic processes
Gas pressure arises from the momentum change of colliding particles
Current and circuits build on the electric field concept
Simple harmonic motion of particles generates a travelling wave
The wave model explains reflection, refraction and interference
Superposition of waves produces standing waves
The wave model explains the Doppler frequency shift
Doppler shifts of starlight reveal stellar motion
Gravitational and electric fields share the inverse-square form
Field strength determines the force on charges in motion
Conductors moving in magnetic fields induce an electromotive force
Induction generates the currents that drive circuits
Electric forces bind electrons to the nucleus in the atom
Atomic energy levels are explained by quantum physics
Wave-particle duality links quantum behaviour to wave phenomena
Nuclear structure determines radioactive stability and decay
Nuclear instability underlies both decay and fission
Mass-energy equivalence governs both fission and fusion
Mass-energy equivalence from relativity explains nuclear binding energy
Gravity drives the collapse and fusion that powers stars
